Learned counsel for the parties, on a mutual consensus, submitted that the instant anticipatory bail application may be allowed, subject to the condition that the balance amount to the tune 86 lakhs, which remains unpaid as on date, shall be paid within a period of next three months starting from the date of this (Uploaded on 12/11/2025 at 04:43:55 PM) [2025:RJ-JP:44488] (2 of 3)
[CRLMB-16082/2024] order.

Additionally, learned counsel for the accused-applicants has given an undertaking that the applicants shall pay a sum, amounting to 10 lakhs within a period of next three days, and the remaining amount shall be paid within the next three months, as directed.

It is further agreed between the parties that if all the above-mentioned conditions are fulfilled by the applicants within the specified period, all the proceedings, civil and criminal qua the said amount shall be withdrawn.

1 3.

Having heard the submissions of the counsel for the parties and looking to the overall facts and circumstances of the matter at hand, prima facie, it appears that the initial registry was executed for a consideration of 88 lakhs.
Thereafter, the applicant transferred the aforesaid registry to father in-law and has obtained loan from a bank, to the tune of approximately 2.45 Crore.
It is thus apparent that there has been intentional suppression of the actual transaction value.

Therefore, on the lines of the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case titled The Correspondence RBANMS Educational Institution v. B. Gunashekar and anr.: 2025 INSC 490, the matter at hand is accordingly referred to the Income Tax Department for necessary action, in accordance with law.

District Jaipur City (East) in F.I.R. No. 363/2024 is directed that in the event of arrest of the accused-applicants Neha Bumb W/o Shri Mohit Kumar Bumb & Anil Kumar Jain S/o Shri Tara Chand Jain shall be released on bail, provided they furnish a (Uploaded on 12/11/2025 at 04:43:55 PM) [2025:RJ-JP:44488] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-16082/2024] personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/-
with two sureties in the sum of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the S.H.O/I.O/Arresting Officer of the concerned Police Station on the following conditions:-
(i) that the applicants shall make themselves available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required;
(ii) that the applicants shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the court or any police officer, and (iii) that the applicants shall not leave India without previous permission of the court.
(SAMEER JAIN),J JKP/255
